headline: SpaceX surpasses Amazon in valuation, hits $2.7T
summary: The space exploration giant's stock price surged, making it the fifth-most valuable company globally, despite Amazon's significant profits.
details: SpaceX has achieved a valuation exceeding $2.7 trillion, surpassing Amazon and becoming the fifth-most valuable company worldwide. This milestone follows a 20% stock price increase on Monday and an additional 8% rise in early trading Tuesday.

This surge in valuation comes despite Amazon reporting a $78 billion profit on $717 billion in sales last year, while SpaceX incurred a $4.9 billion loss on $18.7 billion in revenue. SpaceX has recently expanded its revenue streams through compute leasing deals with AI companies Anthropic and Google.

The company's valuation has seen a dramatic increase, adding $1 trillion since its IPO on Friday. SpaceX debuted with a valuation of approximately $1.7 trillion, raising nearly $86 billion in its initial public offering.

A significant factor contributing to the recent stock jump is SpaceX's acquisition of AI coding startup Cursor in an all-stock deal valued at $60 billion. This acquisition follows a collaboration announced in April, which CEO Elon Musk stated was part of a rebuilding effort for his AI company, xAI, now integrated into SpaceX.
Experts had predicted that SpaceX's stock might experience volatility due to only about 4% of its total shares being made available for trading.
